prompt:
Design a printed project box and its lid: two parts, `enclosure` and `lid`. It is going on an FDM printer, so nothing may be thinner than the process minimum wall of 1.6 mm. All the numbers below are in `globals.py` - read them through `hc` instead of repeating them.

`enclosure` is the box: an 80 x 60 mm footprint centred on the origin, 30 mm tall standing on z = 0, hollowed out from the top. The side walls are 2 mm thick and the floor is 2.5 mm thick, so the cavity is open at the top and runs from z = 2.5 up to the rim.

Inside it stand four screw bosses, one at each of x = +/-30, y = +/-20. Each boss is an 8 mm diameter column rising from the floor to z = 24, bored with a 3.2 mm pilot hole 15 mm deep down from the boss top. The bosses are free-standing - they do not touch the walls.

`lid` closes it: a 3 mm plate the size of the footprint that seats on the box's rim (so it spans z = 30 to 33), with a register lip 2 mm deep dropping into the cavity below it (z = 28 to 30). The lip is inset 0.2 mm from the cavity wall on every side so the lid drops in without a press fit. Four 3.4 mm clearance holes go straight through the lid on the same pattern as the bosses.

The project also contains `wall_gauge` and `boss_gauge` - reference geometry the acceptance checks measure against. Leave them exactly as they are.

Build both parts, and take a section view through the +Z midplane so the internal bosses are on record.
notes: Difficulty 8. Checks: min wall >= 1.6 mm measured as full containment of the seeded 1.6 mm shell gauge, boss pattern/height/bore via the four go-pins (0.05 mm radial gap, zero interference), lid/box zero interference with rim contact plus a lid volume pinning the declared 0.2 mm register clearance, exact box material volume, envelopes and topology. Render: a +Z midplane section of the enclosure must exist.
